Implemented the Python Nushell port in [nushell_port.py](/C:/Users/liuliu/Documents/tura_workspace/target/project-rebuild-source-port/r-6439a15214/nushell/codex-main-1/workspace/nushell_port.py), with entrypoints:

- [compile.sh](/C:/Users/liuliu/Documents/tura_workspace/target/project-rebuild-source-port/r-6439a15214/nushell/codex-main-1/workspace/compile.sh)
- [executable.py](/C:/Users/liuliu/Documents/tura_workspace/target/project-rebuild-source-port/r-6439a15214/nushell/codex-main-1/workspace/executable.py)
- [executable.cmd](/C:/Users/liuliu/Documents/tura_workspace/target/project-rebuild-source-port/r-6439a15214/nushell/codex-main-1/workspace/executable.cmd)

The implementation covers `nu -c` expressions, pipelines, records/tables, JSON/CSV/NUON conversion, strings, math, ranges, selection/filtering, and common filesystem snippets.

Verified:
- `python -m py_compile nushell_port.py executable.py`
- Byte-level comparison batch through `executable.cmd` against the official `nu.exe`: `failed 0`

I could not execute `compile.sh` locally because this Windows image does not have `sh`/`bash`, but the script is POSIX `sh` compatible and creates the required entrypoint shape.
